problem: Foundation visual navigation models such as ViNT and NoMaD use static, scene-agnostic transformer decoders that process all features and activate all layers. This is computationally heavy for edge robots and works as a black box.
motivation: Robots need efficient and explainable navigation. Humans recruit resources according to task complexity, so simple scenes should need fewer features and layers than complex ones. The paper asks whether all decoder layers and all pixels are actually needed.
key_idea: Combine a Gumbel-Softmax hard feature selector (sparse tokens) with a feature-aware early-exit transformer decoder, whose exit thresholds are tuned by constrained Bayesian Optimization, so compute adapts to scene complexity.
insight: The feature selector sparsifies tokens and stabilizes early exit: the dynamic decoder alone saves FLOPs (2.41) but loses accuracy (Sim_a 93.68 vs 94.49), while adding the selector gives 1.93 GFLOPs and higher accuracy (94.92). Bayesian optimization matters: without BO, FLOPs are 2.46 vs 2.11 with BO, and SR is lower. Exiting before the decoder saves more compute but slightly lowers accuracy. Harder scenes (outdoor, CARLA Scene C) use more FLOPs, consistent with adaptive compute.
method: Encoders: two EfficientNet-B0 instances; one encodes the observation sequence (5 past frames), the other encodes the early-fused current observation and goal image. Encoded features are used as tokens directly, without ViNT's 1280-to-512 MLP projection.

Dynamic hard feature selector: an MLP projects features to 2x dimension, then a pixel-wise Gumbel-Softmax with temperature tau gives binary masks for the observation and goal features. The masks are trained end-to-end, are sparse and give saliency maps.

Dynamic transformer decoder: a 4-layer, 4-head decoder with intermediate predictions. Stochastic early-exit is used in training, and a shared prediction head (4-layer transformer + MLP) outputs action and waypoints.

Feature-aware early exit: follows DeeR-VLA's action-consistency criterion, ||h(x_i) - h(x_{i-1})||_2 <= eta_i. It adds an aggressive pre-decoder exit that skips the whole decoder when the observation-goal L2 difference is below a threshold tied to masked pixel counts.

Bayesian Optimization of thresholds: after training, thresholds eta are found by maximizing cosine similarity of action and waypoint to ground truth, with penalty terms for time, peak GPU memory and FLOPs constraints.
Training loss: log-likelihood of ground-truth action and lambda-weighted waypoint distance (lambda=0.5), trained with the ViNT setup.

setting.backbone: EfficientNet-B0 + 4-layer transformer decoder with Gumbel-Softmax feature selector (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: ViNT-style data; trained from scratch per dataset (Recon, Go-Stanford, SACSoN, SCAND, random 80/20 split), 100 epochs; CARLA fine-tuning on 200 Town01 trajectories, 80 epochs
setting.observation: monocular RGB (85x64) with 5 past frames + goal image
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints and action angle (relative waypoints, tracked by a PID controller in CARLA)

numbers_note: No standard VLN or ObjectNav benchmarks; evaluation is on offline datasets (with a random 80/20 split, since no official split is given, so 'test' is used) and CARLA. Abstract's 2.26x FLOPs, 42.3% time and 32.8% memory are summary figures. Table 1 SCAND Sim_w is 97.03, but Table 8 (Mamba comparison) prints 97.43 for Ours.
results: Compared to ViNT, DynaNav uses about 58% fewer FLOPs (1.93 vs 4.37 GFLOPs on Recon) with similar or better similarity (Recon Sim_a 94.92 vs 94.49). NoMaD is slightly more accurate on some sets but needs about 4x the FLOPs. In CARLA, DynaNav matches ViNT's success rate (0.727/0.664/0.588 vs 0.724/0.659/0.589) at less than half the FLOPs, and is far above GNM (~0.25-0.30).
limitations: Needs an extra post-training Bayesian Optimization stage with manually set constraints, which costs effort.
Evaluated on offline datasets and CARLA only, with no real-robot tests. Gains over ViNT in accuracy are small, and NoMaD could not be run in CARLA.
Pre-decoder exit trades accuracy for efficiency; the exit criterion is a single unified threshold across scenes.
